data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 rejects the distinction between genuine reliability gain and mere compliance as a false dichotomy, arguing that for objectively verifiable tasks any compliance that tracks the right answer is a genuine gain by definition. But the problem explicitly asks 'what evidence within a single evaluation would distinguish a genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance that happens to track the right answer,' so SRC_002 refuses the question rather than answering it. Its counterconditions only cover generalizability and overfitting; they do not handle the within-evaluation, same-distribution case the prompt asks about, namely that the checklist happens to track the right answer for reasons unrelated to the panel's underlying reliability.
